open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app — unauthenticated documentation
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token; it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers, and holds no credential, server path or project data.
open_points.question: Are these three HTTP operations exceptions to A5 rule 1, which says every operation except the health answer requires exactly one Authorization field, or must they return an M08 unauthorized refusal without a valid token?
options: Serve all three documentation operations without authentication
Require the token for all three documentation operations
Treat them as non-operations and state explicitly why A5 rule 1 does not apply
open_points.default_guess: Serve them without authentication because the changed passage says so explicitly, and amend A5 rule 1 to name the exception.

witness.initial: The service is listening and the caller has no Authorization field.
events: An HTTP caller sends GET /openapi.json without an Authorization field.
outcomes: The framework returns the generated OpenAPI description without a token.
A5 rule 1 applies and deliverer_api returns 401 with the unauthorized M08 before anything else is examined.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app — route set
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token; it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers, and holds no credential, server path or project data.
open_points.question: Does the HTTP surface contain exactly the four routes in the Outputs table, or seven reachable routes including these three documentation paths, and are the documentation paths governed by the statements about served routes and wrong methods?
options: The complete route set is seven routes
There are four application routes plus three explicitly excluded framework endpoints
The documentation paths replace or alias routes in the four-route surface
open_points.default_guess: Describe four application routes plus three framework endpoints and state which route-wide rules apply to each.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app — documentation endpoint methods
open_points.text:
The framework also serves its generated description of the four routes at
`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` without a token; it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers, and holds no credential, server path or project data.
open_points.question: Which HTTP method or methods are accepted at each documentation path, and therefore which requests to those paths receive 405?
options: GET only at all three paths
GET and HEAD at all three paths
Use whatever methods the selected framework registers
open_points.default_guess: GET only, with every other method receiving 405.

outcomes: POST is not a registered method and receives 405.
The documentation resource is served because the text fixed only its path, not its accepted method.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app — routing error responses
open_points.text:
A path that is not a route answers 404, and a route's path with another method answers 405, both with the
framework's own body and not M08.
open_points.question: What exact status body, media type, and required headers constitute the public 404 and 405 responses, including whether a 405 carries an Allow header?
options: Fix the exact JSON bodies, content type, and headers in this contract
Adopt the pinned framework version's untouched default responses as an explicit version-dependent contract
Leave bodies and headers outside the public contract and specify only status codes
open_points.default_guess: Use the pinned framework's untouched defaults and explicitly require its normal Allow header on 405.

witness.initial: The service is listening with the four application routes and documentation endpoints.
outcomes: A framework configuration returns JSON error bodies and an Allow header for the method error.
Another framework-valid configuration returns HTML or plain-text error bodies, or omits a contractually required Allow value, while preserving status 404 and 405.

open_points.subject: public_op:deliverer_router.create_app — generated API description
open_points.text:
it names the routes and the forms of their bodies and
answers
open_points.question: Exactly which request headers, success schemas, M08 schemas and status codes must the generated description declare for each of the four routes, and must it declare the Authorization requirement even though authentication is performed inside deliverer_api rather than by the router's extractor?
options: Describe Authorization plus every success and refusal response of each route
Describe bodies and success answers only
Expose only framework-inferred schemas, even when they omit handler-enforced authentication or refusals
open_points.default_guess: Declare the Authorization header requirement and the complete success and M08 response map for scan, delivery and mark, while declaring health as unauthenticated.

witness.initial: The service is listening and exposes /openapi.json.
events: The generated client invokes the scan route.
outcomes: The description declares Authorization and the client supplies the bearer token and understands M08 responses.
The description omits Authorization because authentication is checked inside the handler, so the generated client sends no token and receives unauthorized.
